title: A history of each question’s changes

items.text: Every question now keeps a history: select it, then History in the right panel. It lists each change saved from this update on — who made it, when, which setting, and what it was before and after.

Put back returns a change to how it was. It first shows each setting now and after, then saves it like any edit, so Undo reverses it. A change of type or a move is listed but not put back — change the type or drag the question instead.

title: Signatures, and what each question type can do

items.text: A Signature question can now be answered: people sign with a finger, a pen or the mouse, on the web form and in manual entry. The signature shows on the response page and in the response PDF.

Help → Builder reference → What each type can do: a table of every question type and where it works — the builder, the web form, manual entry, paper and scan, the PDF, spreadsheets, Google Sheets and Airtable, analytics and conditions.
The “Adv” mark in the question list now says what it means: the type works like any other, and its settings are more technical.
A photo, file or signature in a spreadsheet export now has a link to open it; you sign in to open it.

title: Philippine places, and choices narrowed by another form

items.text: A Cascading select can use the Philippine Standard Geographic Code (PSGC) from the Philippine Statistics Authority: Levels tab → Philippine places (PSGC). It gives Region, Province or district, City or municipality, and Barangay, from the 3Q 2026 list. When a level has only one choice, such as a city outside any province, it fills itself in.

Show only the choices another form has answers for — for example, only the barangays with a report in another form — or only those with none yet. Set it with Show only, on a cascade level or on a question whose choices come from a list file or another form.
Manual entry opens faster for forms with long choice lists: the lists now load beside the page.

title: Grids from lists, and sections as tables

items.text: A Grid's or Likert matrix's rows can come from a list file or another form's answers: Grid tab → Rows come from. A grid column's choices can too. They are copied in when you publish; publish again to pick up new answers.
Add and rename a grid's rows and columns right in the builder's Preview.

A repeatable section can be laid out as a table: each question is a column and each entry a row, with Add row and Remove row. Phones still show one card per entry. Section → Advanced → Layout → Table.
The response PDF and the paper form draw a table section as a table.

title: Choices from lists and other forms

items.text: Multiple choice questions can take their choices from another form's answers, as Single choice and Dropdown already could.
Upload a list as a CSV or Excel file and use it for a Single choice, Multiple choice or Dropdown question: Options → Choices come from → A list file.
Short text questions can suggest answers as people type, from a list file or another form's answers. Any other answer is still accepted.
The builder's Preview shows choices from a list file or another form. A long list shows its first 200.
Excel turns a code like 01 into 1. The upload now says how to keep codes as text.
Grids: give each column its own type (one choice, several choices, text, a number or a date) and its own list of choices.
Grids and Likert matrices are drawn as tables on computers and tablets, and as cards on phones.
A Likert scale is drawn as one line of points with the words underneath.
Spreadsheets, Google Sheets and Airtable get a column for every grid cell, beside the usual summary column.
The printed form shows each grid cell's choices as tick boxes, and a writing box for text, numbers and dates.

title: Small fixes for a tidier, more consistent look

items.text: Error messages are easier to read in dark mode, in one shade of red everywhere, including the forms people fill in.
Dialogs space their paragraphs evenly, such as Move scope and Delete scope.
Point at a cut-off name, web address or reply to read it in full.

title: Version numbers, What's new, and the testing rounds so far

items.text: Version number in the sidebar, under every page and on the sign-in page.
What's new opens after you sign in when something changed; always one click away at the foot of every page.
Feedback: tag a report as a bug, a suggestion or a question, and follow every testing-round comment under Feedback & testing.
The builder: insert a question into a formula or a label, use another question's answer as a limit, and build a calculation from presets such as Age and Join answers.
Default values fill in when a form opens, and Today follows the form's time zone.
